objective: By the end of this lesson you can run the before-takeoff check from the POH checklist, explain why each item is checked, spot a bad engine or system before takeoff, and brief your takeoff out loud with a plan for an engine failure.
why: About twenty percent of yearly GA accidents happen during takeoff and departure climb [[24:133|AFH 6-1]]. The run-up is your last chance to find a problem while you are still safely on the ground.

prereading.what: Before-takeoff check, run-up spot, systems to check, takeoff briefing, takeoff checks.

prereading.what: Carburetor ice and carb heat, ignition system and the magneto check, oil pressure.

warmup: You add run-up power, switch to the left magneto, and the rpm does not drop at all. Is that good news or bad news?

key_terms.def: The systematic AFM/POH check of engine, controls, systems, instruments and avionics before flight [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
The before-takeoff engine check, done at a run-up spot near the takeoff end of the runway [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
Switching from BOTH to RIGHT, then BOTH to LEFT and watching the rpm drop, to find ignition problems [[1:175|PHAK 7-15]].
Anti-icing system that preheats air before the carburetor; checked during the run-up [[1:170|PHAK 7-10]].
Shows the vacuum that spins the attitude and heading indicator gyros [[1:218|PHAK 8-16]].
Shows if the alternator is making enough power and if the battery is charging [[1:191|PHAK 7-31]].
A spoken plan for the takeoff, including what you will do if the engine fails [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].
Wingtip vortices from another aircraft; strongest when it is heavy, clean and slow [[1:106|PHAK 5-9]].
A takeoff from a taxiway intersection instead of the runway end, so less runway is left [[33:253|AIM 4-3-10]].
No talk or actions unrelated to the flight during taxi, takeoff and landing [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.5]].

chunks.title: Why we do a before-takeoff check

body.p: The before-takeoff check is the systematic AFM/POH procedure for checking the engine, controls, systems, instruments and avionics before flight [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]. Its job: prove the airplane is in safe condition, the way the manufacturer says, before you commit to the runway.
The checklist lives in the POH Normal Procedures section (Section 4). That section includes a before-takeoff checklist and an Amplified Procedures area with more detail [[1:234|PHAK 9-4]].

bullets: A checklist is a memory aid so critical items are not forgotten [[24:36|AFH 1-15]].
Before takeoff is one of the phases that should always have a prepared checklist [[24:36|AFH 1-15]].
Each airplane is different, so use that airplane's own AFM/POH before-takeoff checklist [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

callout.text: Pilots who don't take checklists seriously get complacent and rely on memory. Without discipline, the odds are on the side of error [[24:36|AFH 1-15]].
Consistent use of approved checklists is a sign of a disciplined, competent pilot [[1:234|PHAK 9-4]].

check.q: Where do you find the before-takeoff checklist for your airplane?
check.a: In the AFM/POH Normal Procedures section (Section 4) [[1:234|PHAK 9-4]].

chunks.title: Pick and set up the run-up spot

body.p: Normally you taxi to a run-up spot near the takeoff end of the runway. The taxi usually warms the engine, but check oil temperature is in range before using high power [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

head: Do this
Why
rows: Choose a firm, smooth spot free of debris
The prop can throw pebbles and dirt back. Chips in the prop make stress risers that can crack a blade [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Stay clear of other aircraft and the taxiway
So you don't block or hit anyone [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Nothing behind you
Prop blast can damage things behind the airplane [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Head as nearly into the wind as you can
Cuts cylinder overheating on the ground [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Roll forward a little, then stop
Lines the nosewheel or tailwheel up with the airplane [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]

body.p: Air-cooled engines get little cooling air on the ground. Long ground runs can overheat cylinders before oil temperature rises, so watch cylinder head temperature if you have it and set cowl flaps per the POH [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

callout.text: Firm, Clear, Into wind, Nose straight.

check.q: Why should you avoid a gravel or debris-covered run-up spot?
check.a: The prop picks up loose objects and throws them back, damaging the prop (stress risers that can crack it) and maybe the tail [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

body.p: Always follow your POH checklist. Most airplanes check and set at least these items [[24:58|AFH 2-21]] [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]:

head: Item
What you check and why
rows: Fuel system
Set per POH, ON, correct tank selected [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Trim
Set for takeoff (elevator, and rudder/aileron trim if you have them) [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Flight controls
Full aileron, elevator and rudder travel in all directions. Less than full range is not acceptable [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Engine
Temps and pressures normal; magnetos within limits; carb heat works [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Electrical
Voltage in range and battery charging [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Vacuum
Acceptable vacuum, typically 4.8 to 5.2 "Hg at 2,000 rpm (use POH values) [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]
Flight instruments
Set for departure; heading indicator agrees with the magnetic compass; heading bug on runway heading [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]
Avionics
Frequencies, navigation, autopilot, transponder set [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]
Takeoff briefing
Out loud, even alone. Include a check of the correct runway and direction [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]

body.p: Then, as you bring in full power on the runway, run the takeoff checks [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]:

bullets: Runway numbers agree with the compass and heading indicator.
Doors latched, windows closed as required.
Controls set for any crosswind.
Power correct, rpm normal, engine smooth.
Engine instruments normal and in the green.

body.p: The ACS Skills for this Task have no number tolerances. This is the standard you are graded on:

head: ACS standard
What it looks like
rows: ACS PA.II.F.S1: Review takeoff performance.
You know the takeoff distance for today and that the runway is long enough
ACS PA.II.F.S2: Complete the appropriate checklist(s).
POH checklist read and done, nothing skipped
ACS PA.II.F.S3: Position the airplane appropriately considering wind direction and the presence of any aircraft, vessels, or buildings as applicable.
Firm, clear spot, into the wind, nothing behind
ACS PA.II.F.S4: Divide attention inside and outside the flight deck.
Regular looks outside during the check
ACS PA.II.F.S5: Verify that engine parameters and airplane configuration are suitable.
Every reading within POH limits; trim, flaps, fuel set for takeoff

callout.text: All run-up and pre-takeoff items should be done before taxiing onto the runway. At minimum before every takeoff: engine instruments checked, and controls full, free and correct [[24:133|AFH 6-1]].

check.q: What does the AFH say about moving the controls only part of the way?
check.a: Pilots often don't use the full range, and that is not acceptable. Check full deflection in all directions [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

chunks.title: Finding engine problems: mags and carb heat

body.p: The engine has two magnetos. Each fires one of the two spark plugs in every cylinder, so if one fails the other keeps working [[1:175|PHAK 7-15]].
During the pretakeoff check, move the switch from BOTH to RIGHT, back to BOTH, then to LEFT. A small rpm drop is normal; the allowed drop is in the POH [[1:175|PHAK 7-15]].

head: What you see
What it means
rows: Small drop, within POH limits
Normal [[1:175|PHAK 7-15]]
Drop more than allowed, or engine quits on one mag
Do not fly until fixed. Could be fouled plugs, broken or shorted wires, or bad timing [[1:175|PHAK 7-15]] [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]]
No drop at all
Not normal. Don't fly [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]]

body.p: Check carburetor heat during the run-up [[1:170|PHAK 7-10]]. Heat lowers power, sometimes up to 15 percent, because warm air is less dense [[1:170|PHAK 7-10]]. On a fixed-pitch prop with no ice, rpm drops and stays steady; if ice was there, rpm drops then slowly rises as it melts [[1:170|PHAK 7-10]].

callout.text: Carb ice is most likely below 70 °F (21 °C) with humidity above 80 percent, but can form at up to 100 °F (38 °C) and humidity as low as 50 percent [[1:169|PHAK 7-9]].

check.q: On the mag check, the rpm doesn't drop at all on either magneto. Fly or not?
check.a: Not. "No drop" is not normal and the airplane should not be flown [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]].

head: Gauge
Normal
Trouble sign
rows: Oil pressure
In the green arc [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]]
Red line means minimum or maximum pressure [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]]
Oil temperature
At least the POH minimum before high power [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Below minimum: wait before high power [[24:58|AFH 2-21]]
Ammeter
Plus side shows battery charging [[1:191|PHAK 7-31]]
Full-scale minus: alternator problem. Full-scale plus: regulator problem [[1:191|PHAK 7-31]]
Suction gauge
Typically 4.8 to 5.2 "Hg at 2,000 rpm [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]
Low suction: attitude and heading indicators may be unreliable [[1:218|PHAK 8-16]]

body.p: Some airplanes have a warning light instead of an ammeter, or a low-vacuum warning light [[1:191|PHAK 7-31]] [[1:218|PHAK 8-16]]. Learn what yours has.

callout.text: A hasty taxi and run-up may not give mechanical gyros time to spin up and read right. Departing into IMC that way is unadvisable [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

check.q: During the run-up the ammeter shows a full-scale minus reading. What does that mean?
check.a: An alternator/generator malfunction; consult the POH [[1:191|PHAK 7-31]].

chunks.title: Review takeoff performance and brief the takeoff

body.p: The rules require you to know runway lengths and your takeoff and landing distance data before every flight [[35:350|14 CFR 91.103]]. Check the POH performance charts and decide if the airplane can safely take off and climb here, today [[24:133|AFH 6-1]].

head: Factor
Effect on takeoff distance
rows: High density altitude
Less engine and prop performance, longer roll, weaker climb [[24:133|AFH 6-1]]
10% more weight
At least 21% more takeoff distance [[1:271|PHAK 11-15]]
Headwind 10% of takeoff speed
About 19% shorter [[1:271|PHAK 11-15]]
Tailwind 10% of takeoff speed
About 21% longer [[1:271|PHAK 11-15]]
Grass, mud, snow, standing water
Longer ground roll [[1:268|PHAK 11-12]]

body.p: Pick a point on the runway where you must be airborne. If you aren't flying by then, abort. POH ground roll plus landing roll gives a good estimate of the runway needed to speed up and then stop [[24:146|AFH 6-14]].
Then give the takeoff briefing out loud [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]:

bullets: Type of takeoff, runway, wind, rotation speed (VR).
Initial turn and climb altitude.
Engine failure before VR: reject, brake, stop straight ahead.
Engine failure after VR with runway left: lower pitch, land, brake straight ahead.
Engine failure after VR, no runway left: best glide, no turns below a set altitude, land in the best area.
The altitude (AGL and MSL) below which you will not turn back.

check.q: You have a 10-knot tailwind and lift off at 60 knots. Roughly how much longer is your takeoff?
check.a: 10 knots is about 17% of 60. A tailwind of just 10% adds about 21%, so expect more than that [[1:271|PHAK 11-15]]. Use the POH chart, or ask for a runway with a headwind.

body.p: During the run-up, split attention between inside and outside. If the parking brake slips or toe brakes are weak, the airplane can roll forward unnoticed. Good habit: one item inside, one look outside [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

bullets: Interruptions cause skipped steps: you put the checklist down, then pick up at the wrong spot [[25:81|AIH 3-30]]. After any interruption, back up a step or restart.
Fixation is getting absorbed in one task and ignoring the rest [[25:81|AIH 3-30]].
Do checklists with the airplane stopped [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].
Set up radios before you move; doing it on the roll is the leading cause of heads-down [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.3]].
Keep a sterile cockpit: no talk unrelated to the flight during taxi and takeoff [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.5]].

body.p: ATC may change your runway or offer an intersection. That changes runway length, wind, and your briefing.

bullets: You must judge if the intersection leaves enough runway. If you want the full length, tell ATC [[33:252|AIM 4-3-10a]] [[33:253|AIM 4-3-10]].
Listen for "shortened" on construction runways [[1:369|PHAK 14-35]].
If you can't safely comply, say "UNABLE" [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].
Unsure? Ask "say again" or for progressive taxi [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].
Re-brief: new runway, wind, abort point and emergency plan [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].
Set the heading bug to the new runway and check it before adding power [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

callout.text: Runway confusion often goes unnoticed until after you take off or land on the wrong surface [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

check.q: Tower offers an intersection departure you think is too short. What do you say?
check.a: Tell ATC you want the full length (or "unable"). The pilot is expected to inform ATC [[33:252|AIM 4-3-10a]] [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].

body.p: Wingtip vortices are strongest when the aircraft is heavy, clean and slow, like at takeoff and landing [[1:106|PHAK 5-9]]. Taking off right behind a large aircraft risks a wake encounter and loss of control [[24:133|AFH 6-1]].

head: Situation
What to do
rows: Departing behind a larger aircraft
Rotate before its rotation point, climb above its path until clear [[34:152|AIM 7-4-6]]
After a large aircraft's low approach, missed approach or touch-and-go
Wait at least 2 minutes [[34:152|AIM 7-4-6]]
Not sure where it lifted off
About 3 minutes gives a margin for the wake to break up [[1:106|PHAK 5-9]]
Intersection takeoff behind a large aircraft

Small airplane, same runway: ATC holds you at least 3 minutes ("Hold for wake turbulence"); you may request a waiver. Not required if the intersection is 500 feet or less from where the large aircraft started its takeoff, same direction [[33:253|AIM 4-3-10]]

body.p: Vortices drift with the wind. A 10-knot wind moves them about 1,000 feet a minute [[1:106|PHAK 5-9]]. Near the ground a light quartering tailwind is the worst case [[1:362|PHAK 14-28]].

callout.text: Whether or not ATC gives a wake turbulence caution, the pilot is expected to adjust to avoid serious wake encounters [[34:152|AIM 7-4-6]].

check.q: A jet just departed ahead of you. Where should you lift off?
check.a: Before the jet's rotation point, then climb above its path [[34:152|AIM 7-4-6]].

chunks.title: Plan for an engine failure on takeoff

body.p: Before every takeoff, think through your options if the engine fails: preferred direction for emergency turns based on departure path, altitude, wind and terrain [[24:133|AFH 6-1]].

head: When it fails
What to do
rows: On the runway
Power to idle, max braking, keep straight. Follow the POH [[24:146|AFH 6-14]]
Initial climb
Lower the nose right away to avoid a stall, glide to a landing area, preferably straight ahead [[24:146|AFH 6-14]]
Low, thinking of turning back
Only if trained and enough altitude [[24:146|AFH 6-14]]

body.p: The FAA example: engine fails at 300 feet AGL, the pilot turns back with a standard-rate turn, and ends up 1,016 feet below the runway [[24:356|AFH 18-7]]. Straight ahead or a slight turn is usually the safest option [[24:356|AFH 18-7]].

callout.text: A low-altitude turn back is an unacceptable risk for student pilots and low-time pilots [[24:357|AFH 18-8]].

body.p: Think about the takeoff path: obstacles, runway length, and surface. Anything that isn't hard and smooth makes the ground roll longer [[1:268|PHAK 11-12]].

check.q: Engine quits at 200 feet just after liftoff. First action?
check.a: Lower the nose to keep from stalling and glide to a landing spot, preferably straight ahead [[24:146|AFH 6-14]].

bullets: Not reviewing POH performance charts before takeoff [[24:138|AFH 6-6]].
Not clearing the area before taxiing onto the runway [[24:138|AFH 6-6]].
Not cross-checking engine instruments after adding power [[24:138|AFH 6-6]].
Not moving controls through their full range [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
Eyes inside the whole run-up while the airplane creeps forward [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
Accepting a mag drop over limits, or "no drop" [[1:175|PHAK 7-15]] [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]].
Rushing the run-up so gyros aren't up to speed [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].
Skipping or mumbling the takeoff briefing [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].
Taking off on the wrong runway: heading bug not set or not checked [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

callout.text: If anything is outside POH limits, the run-up just did its job. Taxi back.

check.q: Name two errors the AFH lists that happen before the takeoff roll even starts.
check.a: Not reviewing POH performance charts and not clearing the area [[24:138|AFH 6-6]].

scenario.title: Busy afternoon at the run-up pad
scenario.setup: You're at a towered airport in a carbureted trainer on a warm, humid day. A friend in the right seat keeps chatting. Mid run-up, Ground calls with a question and you set the checklist down. A regional jet just departed Runway 27. When you call ready, Tower says: "Runway 33 at Alpha, intersection departure, wind 290 at 12." You briefed Runway 27 full length.

questions.q: You pick the checklist back up after talking to Ground. What's the trap?
questions.a: Restarting at the wrong place and skipping steps; interruptions are a big source of error [[25:81|AIH 3-30]]. Back up and redo the item you were on. Keep eyes outside too in case the brakes slip [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

questions.q: How do you handle your chatty friend?
questions.a: Brief a sterile cockpit: no unrelated talk during taxi and takeoff [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.5]].

questions.q: Should you accept Runway 33 at Alpha?
questions.a: Only if the remaining length covers your POH takeoff distance; you must judge that, and ask for full length or the distance if needed [[33:252|AIM 4-3-10a]] [[33:253|AIM 4-3-10]]. Wind 290 is 40 degrees off Runway 33, a crosswind. If not safe, say "unable" [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].

questions.q: What about the jet that just left?
questions.a: Its wake sinks and drifts with the wind. It left from a crossing runway, so plan your climb and heading so you never fly below and behind its path. If you are unsure where it lifted off, waiting about 3 minutes gives a margin [[34:152|AIM 7-4-6]] [[1:106|PHAK 5-9]].

questions.q: What must you redo before rolling on the new runway?
questions.a: Re-brief out loud: runway, wind, abort point, engine-failure plan, turn-back altitude [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]. Set the heading bug to 330 and check alignment before adding power [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

questions.q: The rpm dropped a lot on carb heat and then slowly rose. Meaning?
questions.a: Ice was likely there and melted. Warm, humid days can still make carb ice [[1:169|PHAK 7-9]] [[1:170|PHAK 7-10]].

skills.do: Show the examiner the POH takeoff distance for today's runway, weight, density altitude and wind, compare it to the runway, and name an abort point.
skills.practice: Before every lesson, work the POH takeoff chart and say the numbers out loud to your CFI.

skills.do: Complete the POH before-takeoff checklist item by item, without skipping, and the takeoff briefing out loud.
skills.practice: Chair-fly the checklist at home with the POH until the flow is smooth; always read it in the airplane.

skills.do: Stop on a firm, clear spot, nose into the wind if possible, clear of other aircraft and the taxiway, nothing behind, nosewheel straight.
skills.practice: On each run-up, tell your CFI why you picked that spot.

skills.do: Look outside between checklist items and catch any creeping or traffic.
skills.practice: Use the one-item-inside, one-look-outside rhythm on every run-up.

skills.do: Verify oil temperature and pressure, mag drop, carb heat, ammeter and suction are within POH limits, and trim, flaps and fuel are set for takeoff.
skills.practice: Learn your POH limits by heart and say each reading against its limit during the run-up.

quiz.q: During the magneto check, the engine shows no rpm drop on either magneto. What should you do?
options: Fly, but write it up after
Don't fly; no drop is not normal
quiz.why: "No drop" in rpm is not normal and the aircraft should not be flown [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]].

quiz.q: Why should the run-up be done on a firm surface free of debris?
options: To keep the brakes from overheating
So the prop doesn't pick up debris and get chipped
quiz.why: Debris thrown by the prop damages it; chips form stress risers that can lead to blade failure [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

quiz.q: What is a typical acceptable vacuum reading at 2,000 rpm?
quiz.why: Typically 4.8 to 5.2 "Hg at 2,000 rpm; use POH values [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].

quiz.q: A full-scale positive ammeter reading during the run-up most likely means:
quiz.why: Full-scale plus means a regulator malfunction; full-scale minus means an alternator problem [[1:191|PHAK 7-31]].

quiz.q: A headwind that is 10 percent of the takeoff airspeed changes takeoff distance by about:
quiz.why: About 19 percent shorter; the same tailwind makes it about 21 percent longer [[1:271|PHAK 11-15]].

quiz.q: When taking off behind a larger departing aircraft, you should:
options: Rotate before its rotation point and climb above its path
Take off right away before the wake forms
quiz.why: Rotate before the larger aircraft's rotation point and climb above its climb path [[34:152|AIM 7-4-6]].

quiz.q: ATC offers an intersection takeoff. Who must decide if the remaining runway is enough?
quiz.why: The pilot must assess the intersection and tell ATC if they want full length [[33:252|AIM 4-3-10a]] [[33:253|AIM 4-3-10]].

quiz.q: The engine fails right after liftoff at low altitude. What is usually the lowest-risk choice?
options: Land straight ahead or with a slight turn
Make a steep turn to the nearest road
quiz.why: Continuing straight ahead or a slight turn usually represents the lowest risk [[24:356|AFH 18-7]].

takeaways: Use the POH before-takeoff checklist every time; it is the manufacturer's test of a safe airplane.
Run up on a firm, clear spot, into the wind, nose straight, nothing behind.
Mag drop over limits, no drop, or any gauge out of the green: don't fly.
One item inside, one look outside. After an interruption, back up a step.
New runway or intersection? Recheck distance, wind and wake, then re-brief.
Brief the engine failure plan out loud; straight ahead is usually safest.
cfi_notes: Have the student explain the 'why' for each checklist item; examiners probe reasons, not just the flow (K1a).
Watch for heads-down run-ups; ask the student what is happening outside in the middle of the check [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
Interrupt the student mid-checklist with a radio call and see if they skip a step [[25:81|AIH 3-30]].
Make the student quote real POH limits: max mag drop, mag difference, run-up rpm, oil temperature minimum, vacuum range.
Have the student do the takeoff briefing out loud on every flight, including a turn-back altitude for that airplane [[24:59|AFH 2-22]].
Give a surprise runway change on the ground and see if they re-check performance and re-brief.
gaps: Run-up rpm, allowable mag drop and difference, oil temperature minimums, flap setting, VR and best glide are airplane-specific; they come from the POH, not these resources.
None of the resources has a section on unexpected ATC runway changes by name; this lesson builds R2 from AIM 4-3-10, PHAK 14-32 to 14-35, 14 CFR 91.103 and the AFH takeoff briefing.
AFH Figure 18-5 labels the lateral distance 4,480 feet while the AFH 18-7 text says 4,200 feet; the lesson avoids quoting that number.
